findings.title: The component flow and `S` plumbing do not match the existing code
findings.description:
- **No `BenchConfig`.** The only bench input is the frozen `Workload` dataclass (`src/migratory/bench/workload.py:99-112`). `from_dict` has a fixed field list (`workload.py:130-169`) and no place for `S` or `cell_size`.
- **`build_spatial_hash` does not take `cell_size`.** Its signature is `build_spatial_hash(state)` (`quadrants_fused_kernels.py:411`). It does not compute `grid_w` or `grid_h` either. `GpuAgentState.setup` computes them (`quadrants_fused_state.py:150-153`), from `cell_size = max_query_radius * DEFAULT_CELL_SIZE_MULTIPLIER`. The diagram line 91 is wrong, and "No structural changes needed there" (line 80) is wrong too, because `quadrants_fused_state.py` must change.
- **No path from `Workload` to `S`.** `QuadrantsFusedTickRunner.setup(workload)` takes only the workload, and the registry constructs the runner with no arguments (`quadrants_fused_backend.py:71-91`). The design never says where `S` is stored or how it gets from `Workload` to `GpuAgentState`.
- **Two kernel call sites are unaccounted for.** The kernel is launched positionally from `run_fused_tick` (`quadrants_fused_kernels.py:400-407`) and from `QuadrantsFusedTickRunner.tick_once` (`quadrants_fused_backend.py:116-123`). Both must pass `S`. Tests call `run_fused_tick`, so a missed call site breaks them.
- **"Which `query_radius`" is unspecified.** Line 54 says `cell_size = query_radius / S`. The state uses `max_query_radius` across profiles. Per-agent radii can be smaller, but `S` cells must cover the maximum.

An implementer has to invent the config surface, so this is under-specified.

findings.title: An existing knob already provides cell scaling and is not reconciled with `S`
findings.description:
`quadrants_fused_state.py:51-54` defines `DEFAULT_CELL_SIZE_MULTIPLIER = 1.0`. Its comment calls it the "single source of truth shared with the fused kernel so a 3×3 cell walk covers any query".
- Adding `S` creates two interacting knobs, `cell_size = max_query_radius * multiplier` and `cell_size = query_radius / S`.
- If someone sets the multiplier to 0.5 with `S=1`, the 3×3 scan silently under-covers the radius.
- The design should state that `S` replaces or derives from the multiplier, for example `S = ceil(1/multiplier)`.
- It should also update the comment, which becomes false once `S > 1`.

findings.title: The composition claim is arithmetically wrong, and it affects the value of the `S` knob
findings.description:
- **Candidate counts.** The doc says S=3 alone drops candidates "to ~5000" and that both together load "~555". But a 7×7 scan of 555-agent cells loads about 27,000 candidates. Slice 148's own rediagnosis note (`148-notes.rediagnosis.md:108-111`) says ~27,000.
- **Scanned area.** The scanned area is (7·16.7)² against (3·50)², a ratio of 0.6, so S=3 alone gives at most about 1.65× fewer candidates.
- **Not multiplicative.** Once the break fires, work is bounded by about `k_max / in_range_fraction`. `S` adds nothing until the cell holds few enough agents that the cap is not reached in the first cell.
- **Unmeasured overhead.** The break only exits the innermost loop (line 29). After the cap, the remaining drow/dcol iterations still do bounds checks and two `_cell_start` global loads each. That is up to 48 iterations at S=3 against 8 at S=1.
- **Constant bounds become dynamic.** Replacing `range(-1, 2)` with `range(-S, S+1)` turns compile-time-constant loop bounds into runtime ones. "S=1 reproduces slice 145 exactly" holds functionally, but not necessarily for performance or register pressure.
- **Consequence for the default.** Early exit at S=1 may capture most of the gain, and S=3 may be neutral or negative. The design should say that S>1 is justified only if the ablation shows it. It should also guard the outer loops on `k_found < cap` rather than only breaking the inner one.

findings.title: Early exit removes counter-gating, so the four-way ablation in the walkthrough cannot run
findings.description:
- **Duplicate commands.** Step 3's four commands differ only in `--subdivision-factor`. The "baseline, counter-gating" and "early exit only" commands are identical, and so are "S=3 counter-gating" and "both".
- **No switch.** Intervention 1 replaces counter-gating, and the design adds no kernel flag or compile-time toggle to turn the break off.
- **Baseline is not reproducible.** The S=1 baseline will already contain the break, so it will not "reproduce slice 145 ~38 TPS".
- **What to specify.** The design must either add an explicit early-exit toggle kernel parameter, or say that the A2 baseline comes from a pre-change commit and drop the "counter-gating" rows.

findings.title: The gate workload does not match the baseline the design cites
findings.description:
- **The workload is N=100k.** `bench/workloads/mid-flock-50k.yaml:7,11` has `n: 100000` and `world_size: [1536, 1536]`. The A2/A3 gates and the "38 TPS at N=50k" baseline assume N=50k. The slice plan puts N=100k at 11 TPS (`140-slices.simulation-scaling.md:48`).
- **The occupancy figure is from a different geometry.** Slice 148's p99 ≈ 5137 and 256-cell figures come from a ~756×756 world (`148-notes.rediagnosis.md:115`).
- **No override.** `--N` and `--config` do not exist as CLI options, so the walkthrough cannot override `n`.
- **What to specify.** The design should name a workload that actually yields N=50k at the quoted density. It should also record the baseline from that exact workload.

findings.title: Verification commands use CLI flags and entry points that do not exist
findings.description:
- **No `scripts/bench.py`.** Only `scripts/148_smem_vs_dram_microbench.py` exists. The real entry point is `python -m migratory.bench --workload NAME --backend NAME` (`bench/cli.py:17-55`).
- **Missing flags.** `--config`, `--N`, `--ticks`, `--subdivision-factor` and `--parity-check numpy` are not defined. Tick counts come from the workload YAML (`measure_ticks`).
- **Not a plan to add them.** Adding CLI flags is neither scheduled nor specified, and the design states that the flow is config-driven.
- **No new tests.** The design specifies none, so `S` validation, the break, and S>1 parity have no automated coverage. The existing parity test (`tests/bench/test_quadrants_fused_parity.py:42-117`) runs `mid-flock` at the default only.
- **"CPU fallback" does not exist.** Line 126 says A1 and A4 can run on Mac "Metal or CPU fallback". `_select_arch` has no CPU fallback and raises off Linux and Darwin (`quadrants_fused_backend.py:46-62`), and the module docstring says so.

findings.title: Option A leaves the seam as dead code and splits the cap logic across two places
findings.description:
- **The seam can no longer reject.** With `if k_found >= max_neighbors and max_neighbors > 0: break` placed before the call, `get_neighbors_first_k` can no longer return 0. It is not "unreachable". It is called and always returns 1.
- **The cap is now a kernel policy.** The "have we collected enough" decision (`k_found >= cap`) lives in the kernel body and no longer in the seam.
- **The A7 claim does not hold.** The design says the swap point "remains intact". A distance-ranked implementation cannot early-exit on `k_found >= k`, so a future slice must remove the kernel break as well as replace the seam body. State that explicitly, or put the exit decision behind the seam, for example a second `qd.func` `should_stop_scan`.
- **Existing test.** `test_get_neighbors_first_k_is_only_inclusion_function` (`tests/bench/test_quadrants_fused_kernels.py:217-250`) guards confinement of selection logic to the seam. It matches only the substrings `k_found < k_max` and `k_found < max_neighbors`, so a `>=` break passes the test while violating its intent. The design should say how the test is updated.
- **Stale docs.** The kernel docstring lines 164-168 ("counter-gating is used, not break") and line 201 ("3×3") become stale. Neither is listed as a change.

findings.title: Warp-divergence analysis rests on a wrong premise and ignores max-over-warp behavior
findings.description:
- **Thread index is not spatial.** The kernel maps thread `i` to agent id `i` (`quadrants_fused_kernels.py:233`). Only the candidate list is cell-sorted. "Agents with similar spatial index" in a warp is not true, and agents move every tick.
- **Warp time follows its slowest lane.** One lane that never reaches the cap, such as an edge or straggler agent with fewer than 32 in-range neighbors, scans all candidates and holds the whole warp. The saving therefore depends on the fraction of warps containing such a lane, not on the mean.
- **The saving figure is overstated.** "~44,968 iterations avoided" assumes every candidate is in range. The real stop point is about `32 / in_range_fraction`.
- **Low density is admitted but not gated.** Line 27 concedes divergence is larger at low density, yet no CUDA regression gate exists there. Step 2 runs only on Mac/Metal and requires only "comparable". Slice 146 will run this kernel in production at roughly 3.5k agents. Add a CUDA no-regression check on `mid-flock` or `dispersed`.

findings.title: Changing `S` alters which neighbors are accepted, and A4's metrics cannot detect it
findings.description:
- **S=1 break is behavior-preserving.** At S=1 the scan order is unchanged, so the break accepts exactly the same neighbors as counter-gating. The 148 note's claim that "set composition changes" is not true for Intervention 1 alone.
- **S>1 changes the accepted set.** First-k-found is order-biased. It takes the first 32 in-range candidates from the top-left of the scan. With S=3 those first cells lie at the far edge of the radius, whereas S=1 takes them from a 50-wide corner cell. This produces a directional bias that changes with `S`.
- **A4 cannot see it.** A4 compares only mean speed and mean nearest-neighbor distance (A4, line 125). Neither is sensitive to centroid drift or direction. Add a flock-centroid drift metric, or randomise or centre-out the scan order.

findings.title: `S` validation is over-specified and its rationale is wrong
findings.description:
- **The memory rationale is not supported.** The doc says S=8 risks "grid_w·grid_h·cell_count auxiliary arrays past practical GPU memory". `MAX_CELLS_SANITY_CAP = 4_000_000` already exists and raises in `GpuAgentState.setup` (`quadrants_fused_state.py:55,154-160`). At world 1536 and S=8, the grid is ~60k cells.
- **The coverage argument is wrong.** "Larger than the physical neighborhood for any realistic combination" is incorrect, because the (2S+1)² block covers about (2+1/S)·r per side for every `S`.
- **`isinstance(S, int)` accepts `True`.** A bool passes the check.
- **Where the check lives is not stated.** "Config-load time" has no home, because `Workload.from_dict` has no `S` field.
- **Suggested cut.** Validate `S >= 1` as an int in one place, and rely on the existing cell-count cap.

findings.title: The gated configuration (S=3) is not what ships through slice 146
findings.description:
The design makes `S` a bench-config input with a default of 1, and says slice 146 is "unblocked". Production has no `Workload`.
- Unless the default moves, or 146 is told how to set `S`, the live server runs at S=1. That is not the configuration that passes A3 (≥100 TPS).
- Tier 2 delivery depends on 146 using the gated configuration.
- State where production gets `S`, for example a `GpuAgentState` constant.

findings.title: The register-spill check (A5) relies on an unverified measurement method
findings.description:
- **The tool path is unconfirmed.** A5 cites `nvcc --ptxas-info`, and Step 4 cites "`TI_PRINT_KERNEL_STATS=1` or equivalent". Quadrants JIT-compiles, and neither mechanism is shown to exist.
- **Slice 148 found the tools absent on one host.** `148-notes.envelope-measurement.md:26` says `ptxas`, `cuobjdump` and `nvcc` were not installed there.
- **Reuse the proven method.** Slice 148 recorded local memory = 0 for the baseline (`148-notes.rediagnosis.md:25`). The design should reuse that measurement method and name it.
- **Dynamic loop bounds add risk.** The dynamic `S` loop bounds make spill more plausible, which is another reason to specify the method.

findings.title: Verified claims about existing code
findings.description: `quadrants_fused_kernels.py:291` is the innermost `for kk in range(start, end)`. The seam is at lines 155–184 and returns a 0/1 `i32`. `build_spatial_hash` spans lines 411–462. The flocker `max_neighbors=32` and `query_radius=50` match `workload.py:36,45`. The slice plan entry 149 assigns both interventions and the exit criteria (≥5× `force_total`, ≥100 TPS, 20% parity), and the design matches those exit criteria.

findings.title: The NFR is restated correctly
findings.description: The 60 TPS at N=50k Tier 2 target is restated, with a stricter ≥100 TPS gate. This is consistent with the slice plan. The only issue is the workload mismatch recorded above.
